semantic_observations: The selected biome strategy uses two bits per spatial axis, so one biome-section palette container covers 64 logical entries; the palette bit requirement is the ceiling base-2 logarithm of the distinct palette count.

For biome data, a zero-bit configuration uses the single-value palette, one through three bits use the linear palette, and larger bit counts use the global palette. Hash-map palette configurations are part of the block-state strategy and are not on the selected biome route.

A simple palette configuration uses one bit width for both in-memory and stored indices, creates its configured local palette, and does not require repacking. A global configuration uses the registry-backed global palette, carries distinct in-memory and stored bit widths, and requires repacking.

When a target configuration requires repacking, semantic values are read from the prior palette/storage and assigned through the target palette into the target storage without permitting another resize during that copy.

The paletted-container data wire form writes one storage-bit-width byte, then the concrete palette representation, then the raw storage words as a fixed-size long array. Its serialized size is one byte plus the concrete palette serialized size plus eight bytes per raw storage word.

The single-value palette network form carries exactly one global-registry identifier as a VarInt and no local palette-cardinality field; an invalid or absent value is rejected rather than silently defaulted.

The linear palette network form carries its palette cardinality as a VarInt followed by that many global-registry identifier VarInts. Decoding resolves every identifier through the global map and encoded-size accounting is the sum of those exact VarInt widths.

The global palette contributes no palette bytes on read or write, so packed storage values are global-palette indices directly. Encoding uses registry identifiers; an unregistered value maps to index zero in the reviewed id lookup, while an invalid decoded index is rejected.
A light DataLayer represents 4096 four-bit values in exactly 2048 raw bytes; construction from a raw byte array rejects any other byte length.
A homogeneous DataLayer can remain unmaterialized as a default nibble value with no byte array, and it is empty exactly when that unmaterialized default is zero.
Copying a DataLayer preserves an unmaterialized homogeneous default without forcing allocation, while a materialized layer is copied by cloning its raw byte storage.
Requesting raw DataLayer bytes materializes exactly 2048 bytes. A nonzero homogeneous default is expanded by packing that four-bit value into both nibbles of every byte.

The selected LayerLightEventListener lookup is nullable. The production LightEngine route converts the section position to its packed section key and delegates to light-section storage; storage prefers a queued DataLayer for that section and otherwise returns the visible stored layer.
Dummy light-listener behavior is not part of the selected route, and this delegate closure admits no light-propagation, world-generation, or publication-pacing semantics.
